defect: The settled state is misnamed, so done tickets are reported as unbuilt.
Deferred tickets are treated as settled, though their criteria are still future instructions.
A ticket with no status key is read as done and silently skipped.
The sprint preamble above the first ticket heading is never searched.
A sprint-file hit reports its line within the section instead of within the file.
Ticket headings are matched at the wrong level, so every section folds into the preamble.
A ticket heading inside a code fence starts a section.
The start boundary checks punctuation only, so a bare name matches inside a longer name.
The end boundary always passes, so a path matches the start of a longer file name.
A file name two tracked files share still matches bare.
The unique bare file name is never added as a token.
Only the full path is a token, so prose citing a shorter directory suffix is missed.
A path given with Windows separators is not normalized and matches nothing.
Changed planning files are searched for, so the plan reports itself.
A single path that could not be searched is not reported as unsearched.
Untracked files are left out of the changeset read from git.
A failed git command while reading the changeset is ignored and its error text is searched as paths.
Hits exit 1, so a caller reads the review input as a failed gate.
A missing ticket directory throws instead of reading as no ticket files.
An unknown flag is taken as a path and searched.
A failed tracked-file listing drops bare-name matching without saying so.
An absolute path is not made repo-relative, so hits name the absolute path.
A trailing slash is kept, so a directory path never matches a file cited beneath it.
Staged renames are detected, so git names only the new path and the old path a ticket cites is never searched.
An unclosed fence runs to the end of the file, hiding every ticket heading after it.
old: : lines.findIndex((line, at) => at > index && closes(opener, line));

defect: Any marker of the fence's character closes it, so a shorter marker inside a longer fence exposes the fenced example headings.
A ticket file whose name matches no ticket key is skipped, so its work is never searched.
A sprint file whose name matches no sprint key is skipped, so its work is never searched.
Only folders three or more segments deep are matched, so a ticket citing a two-segment folder is missed.
A folder cited with a trailing slash reads as a citation of a child, so the ticket is missed.
One-segment folders are matched, so a ticket citing a top-level folder floods the report.
A folder citation ignores the name boundary, so it matches a sibling that shares its prefix.
A folder followed by a child name counts as a folder citation, so any cited file matches every change in its folder.
A line that names only a folder is printed as naming the changed path, so a reader searching the cited line for that path finds nothing and dismisses a real pending ticket.
A folder cited through a relative link is missed, as a root-relative-only match start would cause.
